stances.claim: EO 43 is the polestar of Aquino's presidency -- it is the executive summary of his vision, mission, goals, values, principles, and methods; upon it, our people will judge him.

The OMB cannot represent the President as offended party in a plea bargain because it is an independent office not under the President's control and supervision; fiscals can (as subalterns of the DOJ Secretary, who is the President's alter ego) but the OMB cannot.

one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban identifies EO 43 -- reorganizing the Cabinet into five clusters (Good Governance/Anti-Corruption chaired by Aquino; Human Development/Poverty Reduction by Soliman; Economic Development by Purisima; Security/Justice/Peace by Ochoa; Climate Change by Paje) -- as the polestar of Aquino's presidency: the executive summary of his vision, mission, goals, values, and methods (transparency, accountability, integrity, leadership by example). He notes VP Binay's magnanimous 'I am a team player' statement despite not heading any cluster. Responding to lawyer Alentajan's letter arguing that the OMB can bind the Republic as offended party in the Garcia plea bargain like regular fiscals, the author rebuts: fiscals are subalterns of the DOJ Secretary who is the President's alter ego -- they can represent the President; but the OMB is a constitutionally independent office, not under the President's control and supervision, and therefore cannot represent him. In the second section, he recounts First Pacific Company Limited's 30-year rise -- from HK$7 million with six employees in a 50-square-meter Hong Kong office in 1981 (co-founded by Manuel Pangilinan and Anthoni Salim) to US$44.57 billion aggregate market cap with 104,000 employees across multiple industries -- celebrated with a dinner-musicale featuring exclusively Filipino performers. The column closes with a tribute to Alejandro Roces -- National Artist for Literature, the author's student-leadership adviser, and Secretary of Education 1961-65 who retained him as legal counsel right after he passed the bar -- who passed away on May 23, 2011 at 86.
